newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends lower on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends lower on rumours.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures closed down on Tuesday mainly on rumours that China's central reserve bureau could be planning to sell copper on the world market, traders said.
An official with the bureau said China had no immediate plans to sell copper as no order had been received from central government authorities to do so.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,380 ($2,819) yuan per tonne, down 290 yuan. It opened down at 23,500, hitting a high of 23,530 and a low of 23,380 yuan.
June fell 190 to 22,780, July 260 to 22,990, August fell 280 to 23,200, October 280 to 23,420 and November 380 to 23,420.
Combined volume rose sharply to 72,210 tonnes from 25,760.
The rumours had no immediate impact on the markets, traders said, but had shaken the confidence of long-position holders in Shanghai.
Weak performance of copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight had added to investor woes, they said.
Three months copper on the LME closed on Monday below $2,500 a tonne, a correction traders on Tuesday said was long overdue and could continue to as low as $2,440.
"These negative factors triggered heavy short-selling, pushing down copper prices in Shanghai on Tuesday, one trader said. "Soft spot prices also contributed to today's falls."

Physical prices are at around 23,200 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, traders said. Technical charts indicated copper futures would continue to fall in the next few days to test the key 23,000-yuan support level, they said.
Aluminium ended down. June lost 50 to 14,950, July 220 to 15,080, September 250 to 15,280 and October 200 to 15,300. August did not trade.
Volume rose to 1,500 tonnes from 650 tonnes.
